acquisition method: the MS/MS spectra were obtained in a data dependent acquisition in the top speed mode
alkylation reagent: samples underwent reduction and alkylation processes using TCEP and iodoacetamide, respectively.
cleavage agent: and then digested with trypsin (Promega) in solution.
collision energy: normalized collision energy 30%; 28% normalized collision energy
normalized collision energy 30%; selected from the full MS spectrum at a 28% normalized collision energy.
fragmentation method: with higher-energy collision dissociation (target 5e4 ions, max ion injection time 40 ms, isolation window 1.6 m/z, normalized collision energy 30%)
instrument: electrosprayed into the Q Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer
ionization type: Peptides eluted from the LC column were directly electrosprayed into the Q Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer
labeling: no labeling strategy mentioned for sample-linked proteomics runs
mass analyzer: electrosprayed into the Q Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer
precursor tolerance: a mass tolerance of 10 ppm for the first-order mass spectrum; Both the precursor and fragment mass tolerances were set to 20 ppm.
fragment tolerance: 0.02 Da for the second-order mass spectrum; Both the precursor and fragment mass tolerances were set to 20 ppm.
ptm: fixed carbamidomethylation of cysteine (C); variable oxidation of methionine (M); variable phosphorylation of serine, threonine, or tyrosine (S/T/Y); variable farnesylation on the C-terminal cysteine (C)

The carbamidomethylation of cysteine (C) was considered as a fixed modification, while the variable modifications encompassed oxidation of methionine (M), phosphorylation of serine, threonine, or tyrosine (S/T/Y), and farnesylation on the C-terminal cysteine (C).
reduction reagent: samples underwent reduction and alkylation processes using TCEP and iodoacetamide, respectively.
